newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium vulnerable after drop.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium vulnerable after drop.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is vulnerable to further losses after Monday's sharp tumble and a test of support around $2,475 is likely, analysts said.
A similar technical scenario prevails in aluminium.
But a strike at Inco's Ontario division, which produces some copper, is mildly supportive for the red metal, traders said
COPPER - Chart-wise, copper's downward correction on Monday below $2,500 was long overdue and looks likely to continue, possibly to as low as $2,440, technical analysts siad.

"(Monday's) fall has taken the RSI to 59.8 from 75.3 on Friday as the overbought market is unwound. Further falls cannot be ruled out with key support seen at the $2,440 level," brokers Brandeis said.
Initially, the market may test nearby support in the area of at Monday's low of $2,475, analysts said.
However, strike action at Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd is certain to offer a bit of help to the market, traders said.
Union officials at Inco's Sudbury operations said on Monday that unionized workers had rejected a tentative contract agreement and would go on strike as of 1201 EDT.
"We've traded a lot of nickel this morning. And for copper, it's obviously more bullish than bearish," a trader said.
"The question is, how low is copper going to go," he said, adding that prices would likely consolidate near term in a range of $2,480-$2,520 before possibly breaking lower.
At 0745 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,498/$2,502 versus $2,485 at Monday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - To some degree aluminium will follow copper, but its technicals suggest further selling pressure is forthcoming, analysts said.
"If $1,595 breaks, falls to $1,587, $1,575 and possibly $1,565 could be seen," said analyst Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading Ltd.
Brokers Rudolf Wolff said the metal's close below $1,600 support on Monday confirmed a head and shoulders reversal pattern with a potential target of $1,538.
"Coupled with the technical indicators trending down, we favour further selling pressure," Wolff said.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was indicated at $1,600/$1,603, versus $1,596 at Monday's kerb close. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
